overview.one_line: Built an IoT-based baby monitoring system that tracks environmental and safety parameters using multiple sensors and wireless connectivity.
overview.summary: Baby Monitoring System is an IoT project developed as part of the Engineering Clinics program. The system monitors important environmental and safety parameters around a baby using sensors for temperature, humidity, sound, moisture, and weight. Sensor data is transmitted wirelessly and displayed through a mobile application, allowing caregivers to monitor conditions remotely. The project provided hands-on experience in embedded systems, sensor integration, wireless communication, mobile application development, and IoT architecture.
overview.elevator_pitch: An IoT-based baby monitoring solution that uses multiple sensors and wireless connectivity to provide real-time monitoring of environmental and safety conditions.

problem.statement: Caregivers often need continuous awareness of a baby's environment, comfort, and safety conditions, which can be difficult to monitor manually at all times.
problem.why_it_matters: Real-time monitoring systems can provide early alerts and improve awareness of environmental changes that may affect a baby's comfort or wellbeing.

motivation.why_i_built_it: The project was developed as part of the Engineering Clinics program, where students were required to build a practical IoT solution using embedded systems and sensor technologies.
motivation.personal_interest: The project provided an opportunity to work with hardware systems, sensors, wireless communication, and mobile applications, which was significantly different from my software and AI projects.
project_goals: Integrate multiple sensors into a single platform

architecture.v1: The system was built around an Arduino-based architecture connected to multiple environmental and monitoring sensors.
architecture.current: Temperature, humidity, moisture, sound, and weight sensors continuously collect environmental data. The Arduino processes sensor readings and transmits information through a Wi-Fi module. A mobile application receives and displays the sensor values through a simple monitoring interface, allowing caregivers to view important metrics remotely.
architecture.future: Future versions may incorporate cameras, AI-assisted monitoring, audio analysis, biometric sensors, predictive alerts, cloud connectivity, and smart-home integration.

implementation_journey.initial_approach: The project began with sensor integration and hardware assembly using Arduino boards and embedded components.
key_decisions: Use Arduino as the primary controller.
Focus on multiple monitoring parameters instead of a single sensor.
Use a lightweight mobile application for monitoring.

challenges.challenge: Integrating multiple sensors into a single system.
challenges.solution: Carefully configured and tested each sensor before combining them into the final architecture.
challenges.lesson: Hardware integration requires extensive testing and troubleshooting.

challenges.challenge: Learning embedded systems and hardware development.
challenges.solution: Worked with Arduino IDE, sensors, modules, and communication protocols through iterative experimentation.
challenges.lesson: IoT development introduces challenges very different from software engineering.

challenges.challenge: Wireless communication between hardware and mobile application.
challenges.solution: Implemented Wi-Fi-based communication for transmitting sensor readings.
challenges.lesson: Reliable communication is critical for IoT systems.

results.current_status: Completed IoT prototype demonstrated during Engineering Clinics and later submitted to the university.
technical_outcomes: Integrated multiple sensors into a single IoT platform.
Successfully demonstrated a working hardware prototype.
project_highlights: One of my few hardware-focused projects.
Combined embedded systems and mobile applications.

lessons_learned: Hardware debugging is fundamentally different from software debugging.
Sensor calibration significantly impacts system reliability.
Wireless communication is a core component of IoT architectures.
Real-world systems often require integration across multiple engineering domains.
Building physical prototypes provides valuable engineering experience.

architecture_decisions.decision: Used multiple sensors instead of a single monitoring parameter.
architecture_decisions.reason: Provided a more comprehensive view of the baby's environment.
Enabled remote monitoring through mobile devices.

architecture_decisions.decision: Focused on practical monitoring features rather than complex analytics.
architecture_decisions.reason: Prioritized reliability and successful hardware integration.
